_about.what: Beacon Assist Protocol Database, demo version 2.1. One protocol per scenario. Prorio reads it to draft proposals; officers suggest changes; a protocol owner approves; every change bumps the protocol's version.
_about.how_written: Every protocol is written in the team's own words. It summarises facts from public pages (each listed under sources) and never copies their text. Steps marked team_design are our own design, not a published rule. See backend/data/PROTOCOLS_SOURCES.md for the copyright approach.
_about.not_real: This is not Westpac's internal procedure. It is a demo built from public information, read on 16 Nov 2026. Facts can change; re-check the source before relying on one.

fields.harm_category: which row of the README harm table this scenario scores under
fields.min_band: gate: the lowest band this scenario may sit in (null = score decides)
fields.clario_can_answer: information Clario may give straight away (Tier 1 or 2), from the customer's data or the knowledge base
fields.protect_first: the protective action Clario offers before queuing (gate G2), always the customer's choice
fields.steps: ordered steps; who = customer, AI (Clario), AI (Prorio) or officer
fields.ai_may: what the AI may prepare or do; anything marked customer-chosen needs a Face ID step-up
fields.officer_must: decisions and actions only a person may take
fields.customer_message: plain-English template Clario sends; placeholders in braces
fields.change_log: what changed in each version and why (present on protocols changed since 2.0)

protocols.title: Customer is being scammed right now or pressured to move money

variants.impersonation: Caller or message claims to be the bank, police, government or a known company; creates urgency (account blocked, fines, unusual activity) and asks for money, codes or a link click.
variants.remote_access: Someone has asked the customer to install software or let them control their device, then coaches them through transactions or a fake 'refund'.
variants.payment_limit_coaching: Customer is being told to raise their daily payment limit. Scammers commonly coach this step.

clario_can_answer: The bank will not ask you to move money to keep it safe, click a link, or share a one-time code.

protect_first.say: Please don't send any money and end contact with that person. I can turn on SafeBlock now: it stops new payments, transfers, card purchases and ATM withdrawals, while scheduled payments and money coming in keep working.

steps.step: Tell the customer to stop contact and send nothing more; if a remote-access app was installed, tell them to disconnect it
Turn on SafeBlock (Face ID step-up)
Ask at most two questions: is someone in contact right now, and has money already left?
Draft a recall for each linked outgoing payment and a scam report
Warm handoff; confirm the story; submit recalls and the report; reset passwords and replace cards where needed
Warn about follow-up 'recovery' offers that ask for fees
Send the case reference, what happens next, and the IDCARE and cyber.gov.au reporting options

officer_must: submit recalls and the scam report
required_checks: Face ID before SafeBlock
gate G1: P1 needs at least one verified account signal
protocols.customer_message: SafeBlock is on and a fraud specialist is working on case {case_id}. We'll try to stop or recover the payments, but recovery isn't guaranteed. Don't pay anyone who offers to get your money back for a fee.

timeframes.rule: Weekly email updates; most cases resolved within 21 days, complex ones take longer

protocols.notes: SafeBlock can be turned off by the customer in the app once they're ready. Beacon's AI never turns it off.

protocols.title: Customer has already paid a scammer (investment, romance, job, fake invoice)

variants.investment: Promises of high or guaranteed returns, pressure to invest quickly, unfamiliar platforms or apps.
variants.romance: Online relationship that moves fast, avoids video calls, then asks for money or banking access.
variants.job_or_unexpected_money: Asked to pay for training or starter kits, or told they are owed money or a prize after paying a fee.
variants.payment_redirection: An invoice or message changed the account to pay into (common with suppliers, tradespeople and property deposits).

clario_can_answer: Don't send any more money, even if asked for fees to release your funds.

protect_first.say: If you've shared any banking details, I can lock your accounts and cards with SafeBlock now.

steps.step: Collect when, how much, how it was paid, and to whom; link the transactions
Draft recalls for recent outgoing payments (recovery is more likely the sooner it's reported) and a scam report
Submit recalls; contact the receiving bank; assess eligibility for any refund
Suggest reporting the loss at cyber.gov.au and talking to IDCARE; encourage telling a trusted person

required_checks: transactions belong to this customer and are outgoing
protocols.customer_message: We've opened case {case_id} and will try to recover the money through the receiving bank. Recovery isn't guaranteed. Please don't send any more payments to this person or company.

timeframes.rule: Weekly email updates; most resolved within 21 days

protocols.title: "Is this call or message really from Westpac?"
clario_can_answer: Genuine calls can come through SafeCall in the Westpac App, which shows the reason for the call; if you miss one, the app tells you which team called.
If you're not sure, get their reference number, end the call, and reach the bank yourself through the app or the number on the official website.
Don't click links, open attachments or install software sent to you.

steps.step: Ask one question first: have you shared any codes, passwords or card details, installed anything, or moved money, or is the person still on the line telling you what to do? If any answer is yes, switch to SCAM_IN_PROGRESS straight away
Check for an open case or a scheduled call from the bank on this customer's record (demo: mock data)
If no record, advise not to act on the contact; offer SafeBlock if details were shared
Safety net: if account signals appear (new payee, unusual transfer, recent detail or device change), re-route to SCAM_IN_PROGRESS

protocols.customer_message: We have no record of contacting you about this. Please don't act on it. If you shared any details, I can lock your accounts now.
protocols.notes: Answers a real customer complaint: people can't tell genuine bank contact from scams. Scored as a general question because asking is the safe behaviour we want to encourage, and nothing is at risk yet; once anything is at risk, the case becomes SCAM_IN_PROGRESS and is scored as one.

change_log.change: Harm category SCAM_IN_PROGRESS -> GENERAL, so a plain 'is this real?' no longer ranks at P2 ahead of real cases. Danger cues now switch to the scam path immediately (Clario), with account signals as a safety net (Prorio).

protocols.title: Card transaction the customer didn't make
clario_can_answer: Merchant names on statements can differ from the shop's trading name; Clario shows the merchant details first.

protect_first.say: I can lock your card now so nothing else goes through.

steps.step: Show merchant details and ask the customer to check with any additional cardholders
Lock the card or turn on SafeBlock
Stop the card and issue a new one with a new number, expiry and security code, linked to the same account
Open the investigation and send the transaction investigation form for the customer to confirm and return within 14 days
Recover from the merchant or refund if eligible under the bank's fraud guarantee

required_checks: Face ID before locking
pending transactions can't be disputed yet: lock and report
protocols.customer_message: Your card is locked and case {case_id} is open. A replacement usually arrives within 5 to 7 business days in Australia, and your PIN stays the same. You'll get the outcome and the reasons.

timeframes.rule: Most resolved within 21 days; complex ones up to 45
Within 21 days, an outcome or written notice that more time is needed; done within 45 days unless exceptional
5 to 7 business days in Australia, 5 to 10 overseas; express courier costs extra

protocols.title: Someone got into online banking and moved money

protect_first.say: I can lock your accounts and cards right now while we look into this.

steps.step: Turn on SafeBlock
Flag recent password, device or contact-detail changes and draft recalls for linked transfers
Reset passwords and telephone banking; try to recover funds via the receiving bank
Assess a refund under the Online Banking Security Guarantee (conditional on the customer having followed the terms)

required_checks: identity verification by an officer
protocols.customer_message: Your accounts are locked and case {case_id} is open. We'll reset your security and try to recover the money. Access may stay blocked during the investigation to protect you.

timeframes.rule: Weekly email updates; most resolved within 21 days

protocols.title: Personal details exposed (data breach, stolen ID, phishing)
clario_can_answer: IDCARE is a free national identity and cyber support service the bank partners with; they help build a response plan.

protect_first.say: If you think someone could use your details to get into your banking, I can lock it now.

steps.step: Check for recent detail changes, new devices or new payees
Strengthen security: password reset, card replacement if card details were exposed
Share the IDCARE option

protocols.customer_message: We've noted that your details may be exposed (case {case_id}). A specialist will help secure your banking. IDCARE can also help you protect your identity.

protocols.title: Locked out of own money, or suspected account takeover

protect_first.say: If you think someone else got in, I can lock your accounts now.

steps.step: Check signal flags: recent password, device or contact-detail changes
Verify identity, then restore access or reset sign-in
Keep the customer updated; offer a callback

required_checks: identity verification by an officer
protocols.customer_message: We're looking at your account access now (case {case_id}). For your safety, only a person can restore it.

protocols.title: Forgotten password or customer ID (no sign of takeover)
clario_can_answer: Self-service reset needs the 8-digit customer ID, date of birth and a registered security device (SMS code or token).
Without those, the bank can reset the password over the phone, any time.

steps.step: Walk the customer through the self-service reset
If they can't, book a callback; if anything looks like a takeover, re-route to ACCOUNT_ACCESS

required_checks: the AI never resets credentials itself
protocols.customer_message: Here's how to reset your password: {steps_link}. If that doesn't work, I can book a call for you.
protocols.notes: Answers to this are often Tier 1. Clario logs out-of-app identity checks it can't do.

protocols.title: Account restricted because identity details need re-confirming
clario_can_answer: Banks must keep customer identity records current. The bank aims to give at least 14 days' notice before restricting access, and a restriction can affect joint accounts too.
Details can be updated in the app (search 'Verify ID' and 'Update contact details'), at a branch, or with the forms sent by the bank.

steps.step: Explain why it happened and the ways to re-verify; check whether electronic verification is available
Mark care needs (older customer, far from a branch, no access to essentials)
Help complete verification and remove the restriction

required_checks: identity verification by an officer
protocols.customer_message: Your account is limited until your ID details are confirmed. You can do it in the app under 'Verify ID', or a specialist can help you (case {case_id}).

timeframes.rule: The bank aims to notify at least 14 days before

protocols.notes: A frequent complaint in public reviews: customers locked out mid-transaction. High value for care-need scoring.

protocols.title: Change of address, phone, email, name or date of birth
clario_can_answer: Email, mobile and address can be changed in the app with a one-time security code.
Name or date-of-birth changes need a branch visit with original documents.

steps.step: Record the request and point to the self-service path; never make the change
Check for takeover signs: recent device or password change, new payees
If assisted: verify identity, then make the change

officer_must: any assisted change to personal or contact details
required_checks: gate G3: never below P3
security code or officer identity check
protocols.customer_message: For your security, contact details change only with your security code or with a person (case {case_id}).
protocols.notes: Looks like admin, but contact-detail changes are a common first step in account takeover.

protocols.title: Request to raise the daily payment limit
clario_can_answer: The customer can change the limit themselves with their security code, for one payment or permanently.

steps.step: Ask one question: is anyone telling you to do this right now? If yes, switch to SCAM_IN_PROGRESS
Otherwise explain the self-service path; the AI never changes limits

required_checks: gate G3
protocols.customer_message: You can change your limit in the app with your security code. If someone is asking you to do this, please stop and talk to us first.
protocols.notes: Scammers commonly coach customers to raise limits.

protocols.title: Card lost, stolen or misplaced
clario_can_answer: Misplaced: lock the card for up to 15 days; unlock any time, or it unlocks itself.
Lost or stolen: report it to cancel and replace. Debit: only that card is cancelled. Credit: additional cardholder cards are cancelled too.

protect_first.say: I can lock your card right now while you check.

steps.step: Ask: misplaced, or lost or stolen?
Check recent transactions for anything unfamiliar; if found, also open FRAUD_UNAUTHORISED
Approve cancellation and replacement to the address on file

required_checks: address on file only (changes go to DETAILS_CHANGE)
protocols.customer_message: Your card is locked. Once approved, a replacement goes to the address we hold (case {case_id}). Your digital card will be ready in the app.

timeframes.rule: Up to 15 days, then it unlocks automatically

protocols.title: Card was declined
clario_can_answer: Common causes: not enough money in the linked account, expired card, wrong card details online, a damaged chip, credit card arrears, or overseas use the bank wasn't told about.

steps.step: Check the customer's own data: balance, card status, expiry, locks, SafeBlock, restrictions
Explain the likely cause from the data; if a fraud hold or restriction caused it, route to that protocol

protocols.customer_message: Your card was declined because {reason}. {next_step}
protocols.notes: Add the care need +10 if the customer can't pay for essentials.

protocols.title: When will my card arrive?
clario_can_answer: Answer from card tracking: dispatched, carrier, status, expected date.
A new account's debit card usually arrives within 5 to 10 business days; a replacement after fraud within 5 to 7 in Australia; an expiry replacement by the end of the expiry month.
The digital card in the app can be used for online and wallet payments meanwhile.

steps.step: Answer from tracking data
If past the expected date, prepare a replacement to the address on file
One-click approve (P4)

required_checks: address changes go to DETAILS_CHANGE
protocols.customer_message: Your card was sent on {dispatched} and should arrive by {expected}. You can use your digital card in the app until then.

protocols.title: How do I activate my card?
clario_can_answer: Search 'Activate' in the app and follow the steps with the card handy.

steps.step: Guide the customer through activation

protocols.customer_message: To activate, search 'Activate' in the app and follow the steps.

protocols.title: Known merchant, wrong amount, or goods or service not received
clario_can_answer: Try the merchant first; check receipts and messages; check with additional cardholders; search the merchant name.
Pending transactions can't be disputed until they finish processing (usually up to 5 business days).

steps.step: Check the transaction is no longer pending; gather what went wrong and any evidence
Draft the dispute
Lodge it; a dispute reference is issued; the bank works with the merchant's bank under card-scheme rules

required_checks: transaction is not pending
protocols.customer_message: Your dispute is being lodged (case {case_id}). Most are settled within about 45 days once we have everything we need, so please send any documents we ask for quickly.

timeframes.rule: Typically about 45 days, counted from when all the needed information is in

protocols.title: Wants to cancel or dispute a pending transaction
clario_can_answer: Pending transactions can't be cancelled or disputed by the bank.
If it's fraud: lock the card or turn on SafeBlock and report it.
If it's a merchant problem: ask the merchant to reverse it, or wait until it finishes processing and then report it.

steps.step: Ask which it is: not mine, a problem with the merchant, or misled into paying
Route to FRAUD_UNAUTHORISED, DISPUTE_CHARGE or SCAM_ALREADY_PAID

protocols.customer_message: Pending payments can't be stopped yet. {route_message}

protocols.title: Stop or cancel a direct debit
clario_can_answer: Search 'Cancel direct debit' in the app; the list shows companies that debited the account in the last 90 days.
If the company isn't listed, the bank can be asked to notify the company or temporarily stop its debits.

steps.step: Guide the self-service cancel
If not listed or not working: notify the company or place a stop

required_checks: debits the customer never authorised go to FRAUD_UNAUTHORISED
protocols.customer_message: You can cancel it in the app under 'Cancel direct debit'. If the company isn't listed, we'll handle it for you (case {case_id}).
protocols.notes: Public reviews mention a chatbot that couldn't handle an unlisted company. The fallback to a person matters here.

protocols.title: Payment sent but not received, or sent to the wrong account
clario_can_answer: Trace = find where the money went when the payee says it never arrived. Recall = try to get it back when it went to the wrong account or was paid twice.
Recalls aren't guaranteed; they depend on the receiving bank and the funds still being there.

steps.step: Decide trace or recall; link the transaction
Draft the trace or recall
Submit it; for a mistaken payment the sending bank asks the receiving bank to return the funds
Explain which rule applies based on how long ago the payment was made

required_checks: the transaction belongs to this customer and is outgoing
protocols.customer_message: We've started a {trace_or_recall} (case {case_id}). Outcomes usually take about two weeks, sometimes up to four. Recovery isn't guaranteed.

timeframes.what: PayID and Osko recall or trace
timeframes.rule: Usually an outcome within two weeks, up to four
Requests the return within 5 business days of the report (best practice: start within 2)
Returned if it's a genuine mistake and the funds are there

timeframes.what: Reported between 10 business days and 7 months
timeframes.rule: Funds frozen; the recipient has 10 business days to show they're entitled
Returned only with the recipient's agreement

protocols.notes: Business customers recalling Osko payments must call or visit a branch.

protocols.title: Wrong BPAY payment
clario_can_answer: Mistaken BPAY payments follow a different process from mistaken bank transfers.

steps.step: Collect the biller, reference and payment details
Handle under the BPAY mistaken-payment process

protocols.customer_message: We've logged your BPAY payment issue (case {case_id}) and a specialist will follow it up.
protocols.notes: needs-verification: the bank-specific BPAY steps were not found in public sources.

protocols.title: PayID locked, misused, or needs moving
clario_can_answer: The bank's help desk can temporarily lock, unlock, close, or move a PayID to another bank.
The bank may lock a PayID itself if it suspects misuse; unlocking may then be restricted.

steps.step: Find out whether it's a request or a suspected-misuse lock
Lock, unlock, close or transfer the PayID

required_checks: misuse locks are reviewed by an officer
protocols.customer_message: A specialist will help with your PayID (case {case_id}).

protocols.title: Customer in financial difficulty
clario_can_answer: Asking early helps: as soon as you're worried about repayments or bills, or income drops.
Options can include flexible payment arrangements, short-term deferrals or reduced repayments, and loan term extensions.
You can apply online (about 15 minutes) or by phone; a financial counsellor is allowed to apply for you.

steps.step: Respond with care; explain support exists and a person will help
Draft notes: what changed, products affected, care cues
Assess and agree any arrangement; suggest free financial counselling

officer_must: the hardship assessment and any arrangement
required_checks: extra care for customers in vulnerable circumstances
protocols.customer_message: Thanks for telling us. A specialist will contact you about support options (case {case_id}). We aim to respond within a week.

timeframes.rule: The bank aims to get back within a week

protocols.title: Domestic or family violence, or financial abuse
clario_can_answer: If you're in immediate danger, call 000. 1800RESPECT offers 24/7 counselling.
The bank has a specialist team for these situations.

steps.step: Prioritise safety; ask only what's needed; don't send notifications that could alert someone else
Discuss protective options: joint accounts set to all-to-sign, reviewing third-party authorities, and, if safe, freezing redraw or additional cards; hardship support

required_checks: safe contact method confirmed before any message
protocols.customer_message: A specialist will contact you only at the time and by the method you choose.
protocols.notes: Gate G7 (README): safety cases never sit below P2 (team_design).

change_log.change: Proposed safety gate adopted in the README as G7.

protocols.title: Customer wants someone they trust to help manage their banking
clario_can_answer: Ways to let a trusted person help: authorised third party (speaks for you by phone), account signatory (manages it in branch), account sharing (separate online profile), or third-party access.

steps.step: Explain the options in plain language
Ask whether the customer is choosing this freely; if anyone is pressuring them, or someone else is asking on their behalf, switch to ELDER_FINANCIAL_ABUSE
Set up the authority after verifying both people

required_checks: identity of both people verified
customer confirms the choice is their own
protocols.customer_message: A specialist can set this up with you (case {case_id}).
protocols.notes: Gate G3: giving another person authority or access changes who can act on the account, so it is officer-only and never below P3, even though it looks like admin.

change_log.change: Split from TRUSTED_PERSON_OR_ELDER_ABUSE v2.0. Routine requests stay officer-only at P3 (G3) instead of sharing a safety-case floor.

protocols.title: Suspected financial abuse of an older customer (reported by the customer or someone worried about them)
clario_can_answer: The bank has a specialist team for these situations.

steps.step: Prioritise safety; ask only what's needed; don't send notifications that could alert someone else
If the person reporting is not the account holder, share no details of anyone else's account; record the concern for the specialist team
Check signal flags on the account holder's record: new payees, unusual transfers, recent detail or device changes
Act on the suspected abuse, including reviewing who has authority or access on the account

required_checks: safe contact method confirmed before any message
protocols.customer_message: A specialist will contact you only at the time and by the method you choose.
protocols.notes: Gate G7 (README): safety cases never sit below P2 (team_design). Money can be leaving through someone the customer trusts, so this is treated like family violence and financial abuse.

change_log.change: Split from TRUSTED_PERSON_OR_ELDER_ABUSE v2.0 and given the P2 safety floor (G7).

protocols.title: Customer has died (family or executor contacting the bank)
clario_can_answer: Anyone can let the bank know, which helps protect the estate from fraud; only the next of kin, executor or a legal representative can manage it.
Notification needs a signed notification form and a certified proof of death. The government's deathnotification.gov.au service can notify several organisations at once.
Funeral costs can sometimes be paid from the estate's funds.

steps.step: Respond with compassion; collect only basic details
Protect the accounts and guide the family through the estate steps

required_checks: authority of the person managing the estate
protocols.customer_message: We're very sorry for your loss. Our estates team will guide you through each step, when you're ready.

protocols.title: Wants help with gambling
clario_can_answer: A gambling block can stop card payments to betting and casino merchants. The primary cardholder can turn it on in the app, online banking or by phone.

protect_first.action: guide the customer to turn on the gambling block
protect_first.say: I can show you how to turn on the gambling block now.

steps.step: Guide the block set-up; share support services
Offer hardship support if repayments are affected

protocols.customer_message: Here's how to turn on the gambling block: {steps_link}. Support is available whenever you want it.

protocols.title: Complaint about service
clario_can_answer: The complaint gets a reference number, a review and an explained outcome. You don't need every detail to start.

steps.step: Capture what happened, when, the outcome wanted, and any reference numbers
Acknowledge, review, respond, and explain the decision and reasons
If unresolved, explain the external option (AFCA)

protocols.customer_message: Your complaint is recorded (reference {case_id}). We'll keep you updated and explain our decision.

protocols.title: Wants to close an account or credit card
clario_can_answer: A personal credit card can be closed in the app; it shows an indicative payout amount, which may not include pending items or interest.
Before closing a deposit account, make sure regular payments are moved and cheques have cleared.

steps.step: Guide self-service closure; check for linked regular payments
If online closure isn't allowed, close it with the customer

required_checks: retention offers are optional; never block or delay a closure
protocols.customer_message: You can close it in the app under 'Close card'. If that isn't available for your account, a person will do it with you (case {case_id}).

timeframes.rule: Instant digital confirmation in the app; by post within 10 business days otherwise

protocols.notes: Public posts describe customers unable to close accounts online and bots hanging up. A one-tap person route matters here.

protocols.title: App or payments not working for many customers
clario_can_answer: Tell affected customers plainly what isn't working, what still works, and when the next update is due.

steps.step: Group cards with the same symptom into one incident (surge mode)
Confirm the incident and approve the customer status message
Send proactive updates; keep individual cards linked to the incident

protocols.customer_message: We know {service} isn't working right now. Your money is safe. Next update by {time}.
protocols.notes: No public bank procedure found; entirely team_design. Motivated by the 10 Nov 2026 outage complaints.
